answer: A seat is a dye recovery on a river reach. The applicant injects 200 grams of rhodamine at the head, files the point, and the node reads the downstream fluorometer, wanting 70 per cent of that pigment back inside nine hours. One reach, one seat, retested biennially. A tributary that swallows the plume before a gauge reads nothing; a copied permit points at water nobody marked. Fifty clones need fifty gauged reaches: fluorometer 5,800 dollars, tracer 900, lab panel 700 a sample, near 400,000 dollars before a curve closes. A sparrow keeps the hedge it sings from, and no hedge grows twice.
